record.paper_title: Projection Algorithms: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: In the specific setting X = ℓ² where C1 is the cone of nonnegative sequences and C2 is a hyperplane with nonempty intersection C = C1 ∩ C2, Fact 3.4 proves that alternating projections always converge in norm. What happens if the hyperplane C2 is replaced by an affine subspace of finite codimension? In particular, does the same norm-convergence phenomenon still hold in that finite-codimensional affine-subspace setting?

evidence.quote: Fact 3.4. [8, Theorem 5.3.(iv)] In X := `2, let C1 be the cone of nonnegative sequences and C2 be an arbitrary hyperplane with C = C1 \cap C2 6= ;. Then the sequence of alternating projections always converges in norm.
Open Problem 2. What happens in Fact 3.4 if replace C2 by an affine subspace of finite codimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \ell^2(\mathbb{N})$ be the real Hilbert space of square-summable sequences. Let
$$C_1 = \{x = (x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \in \ell^2 : x_n \ge 0 \text{ for all } n\}$$
be the closed convex cone of nonnegative sequences, and let $C_2 \subset \ell^2$ be a closed affine subspace of finite codimension such that $C := C_1 \cap C_2 \ne \emptyset$. Denote by $P_{C_1}$ and $P_{C_2}$ the metric projections onto $C_1$ and $C_2$, respectively. Given any starting point $x_0 \in \ell^2$, define the sequence of alternating projections by
$$x_{2k+1} = P_{C_2}(x_{2k}), \qquad x_{2k+2} = P_{C_1}(x_{2k+1}), \qquad k = 0,1,2,\dots.$$
It is known that when $C_2$ is a hyperplane (i.e., a closed affine subspace of codimension $1$), the sequence $(x_k)$ always converges in the norm topology of $\ell^2$.

Question: Does norm convergence of the alternating projection sequence $(x_k)$ continue to hold for every starting point $x_0$ when $C_2$ is allowed to be an arbitrary closed affine subspace of finite codimension (with $C_1 \cap C_2 \ne \emptyset$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem extending a known hyperplane (codimension 1) result to finite codimension. Recent literature on alternating projections in ℓ² with the nonnegative cone and affine subspaces (e.g., works treating codimension-2 cases under additional sign/support hypotheses on the defining vectors) gives only partial results, and no source found resolves the general finite-codimension case. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Convergence rate of alternating projection method for the intersection of an affine subspace and the second-order cone
status_evidence.snippet: Studies alternating projections between affine subspaces and cones, focusing on rates rather than resolving norm convergence for the nonnegative ℓ² cone with finite-codimension affine subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats affine-subspace/cone intersections but does not settle the finite-codimension extension for the ℓ² nonnegative cone.

status_evidence.title: Analytic Formulas for Alternating Projection Sequences for the Positive Semidefinite Cone
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit analyses for PSD-cone alternating projections; does not address the ℓ² nonnegative-sequence cone with arbitrary finite-codimension affine subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: No general resolution of the open problem is provided for the ℓ² nonnegative cone setting.
